evidence: Receiving DO2 48.2h: 2.93 mg/L, falling monotonically to 1.73 mg/L at 52.0h — below minimum_do_mg_l of 2.0
Healthy receiving DO2 ~10.7-11.9 mg/L during 40-48h prior to the excursion
Delayed product assay: P = 1.08 g/L @36h, 3.05 g/L @48h — active production at risk of oxygen limitation
Source batches under similar trajectories maintained DO2 ≥ ~7.4 mg/L (e.g. source-3 74.8h), showing receiving-specific oxygen deficit
Allowed action bounds: combined = [0.8 feed, 1.15 air]
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed from ~11 mg/L to 1.73 mg/L (48-52h), already violating the 2.0 mg/L oxygen floor, while product formation is still active (P 3.05 g/L @48h). A combined bounded intervention (feed ×0.8, air ×1.15) simultaneously reduces oxygen uptake demand and increases transfer capacity, giving the fastest return above the DO2 constraint while retaining product mass. Increase_air alone may recover too slowly given the demand trend; feed reductions alone sacrifice production; stop yields zero production.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters (kLa, OUR kinetics) are unknown, so the recovery rate under combined action is uncertain; DO2 could remain near 2 mg/L for several hours. If the DO2 deficit is driven by an unmodeled factor (e.g., a feed-composition or contamination issue rather than the O2 balance), reducing feed may not fully restore DO2. Residual risk that product quality/yield is modestly affected by temporary feed reduction.

evidence: Receiving DO2 48.0h=10.76 mg/L vs 48.2h=2.93 mg/L, then 1.73-2.9 mg/L through 52.0h — oxygen constraint at 2.0 mg/L breached repeatedly
Receiving P assay at 48h = 3.05 g/L, consistent with all three source batches (2.98-3.06 g/L) — no intrinsic production deficit
Forward model update: estimated_transfer_multiplier=0.439 at change time 48h — severe aeration/transfer capacity loss relative to source

Model comparison: strong_feed_reduction gives post-decision below_limit_h=7.4, min DO 1.17, product mass 172.6 kg vs keep 8.2h/1.03/171.3 kg, increase_air 11h/0.89/171.3 kg, combined 9.2h/0.99/171.5 kg, reduce_feed 10.6h/0.87/171.4 kg
submission.rationale: DO2 collapsed at 48.2h (11 mg/L to ~2.9) and now hovers at the 2.0 mg/L minimum, indicating an oxygen transfer-capacity fault (model-estimated transfer multiplier ~0.44). A 15% air increase alone cannot compensate; the only effective lever is cutting oxygen uptake via feed reduction. Strong feed reduction (0.6x feed + 1.15x air) yields the smallest post-decision oxygen violation (7.4h below limit, min DO ~1.17, deficit 3.8 mg-h/L) and the highest retained product mass (172.6 kg) across all bounded interventions, avoiding a stop (which would count zero production). Even this may not fully restore DO above 2.0 mg/L, so escalation is flagged if DO2 continues to fall.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not the receiving realization; all five sensitivity members remain infeasible for every action, so the intervention reduces but likely does not eliminate oxygen-constraint violation. The exact cause of the transfer loss (fouling, rheology, kla drop) is hidden and could evolve. Delayed P assays lag by 4h, so current product state (48h assay only) is approximate.
